item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports competitive ranking objectives, with caution about false negatives. [PSL, NeurIPS 2024](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/db1d5c63576587fc1d40d33a75190c71-Abstract-Conference.html) identifies exponential softmax weighting as a source of false-negative sensitivity and loose alignment with DCG; alternative pairwise activations provide a tighter surrogate and more balanced contributions. [Hard-BPR, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) modifies BPR specifically to reduce false-negative influence under dynamic hard-negative sampling. Earlier [hard-negative theory](https://doi.org/10.1145/3543507.3583223) connects sampling hardness to partial AUC and Top-K performance, supporting controllable hardness rather than always selecting the highest-scoring unobserved item.\n\nSampled objectives also introduce estimation bias. [Improved Estimation of Ranks, 2024](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/) corrects sampled rank estimates for efficient WARP/LambdaRank training. [Correcting the LogQ Correction, RecSys 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) shows that conventional correction mishandles the deterministically included positive; its revised estimator distinguishes positive and sampled-negative contributions. These findings motivate an experiment, not an established BERT4Rec improvement: first replace the reconstruction objective with candidate-set softmax at masked positions, keeping masking/window sampling fixed. Then separately compare uniform negatives against a uniform/hard mixture selected by the same network, excluding observed training positives and using robust weighting to limit suspected false negatives. Preserve the bidirectional masked backbone and appended-mask inference, with one checkpoint per category. Select solely by the pinned macro validation HR@10; weaker training margins alone cannot establish benefit."}
